DEV_STORYFLOW'S FLEET LOG TRIAGED IN FULL: 26 entries, 16 ALREADY FIXED, 7 OPEN, 3 partial or unverified. Each checked against the running build, not the changelog.

⚠️ FIRST, A CORRECTION THAT COST NOTHING ONLY BECAUSE IT WAS CAUGHT: THIS IS NOT ALEX'S FILE. A standing note claimed "Alex has TWO feedback files; the Aug 7-8 one was never triaged". The Aug 7-8 uploads are dev_storyflow's FLEET LOG — `🔌 api-boss`, `👑 dragon Boss`, numbered workers — with ZERO mentions of Grok or Alex across 754 lines. Alex's Grok file is the 249-line Aug 14 one, already triaged. THERE IS NO SECOND ALEX FILE. Second false premise from my own notes in one day; see [[fact:the-music-graph-feedback-file-is-four-sessions-and-its-first-batch-was-fixed-long-ago]].

⭐ SIXTEEN ALREADY FIXED, and several shipped IN THE REPORTER'S OWN WORDS, which is worth noticing: they asked for `Artifact` to declare `opaque` vs `pending_expansion` and the enum reads exactly `[atomic, opaque, pending_expansion]`; they asked for volatility `stable` vs `append_only`/`living` and it reads exactly `[stable, append_only, living]`. Their `orphan_node`/SPECIFIES escalation is fixed at `heal.rs:872` — the SAME fix that closed music_graph F4, two projects reporting one defect. Their enum-rejection complaint is quoted verbatim in `service.rs:543`. `OWNED_BY` (* → Contributor) answers their accountability ask. The `check-health`-named-first string, filed TWICE ten minutes apart with a fleet-wide STOP-ORDER posted to counteract it, was fixed in #102.

Their served-vs-on-disk staleness pair (20:17 and 20:29) produced `req:the-server-is-the-authority-on-its-own-currency`, and the test file cites their measurement verbatim — four sessions reading `0.22.1` on two days and drawing OPPOSITE conclusions. The worker who proposed deriving it from `/proc/self/exe` being marked `(deleted)` rather than comparing version strings got exactly that mechanism.

SEVEN GENUINELY OPEN, in the order they deserve:
1. A VERIFICATION'S OUTCOME IS PROSE, so a self-contradictory result stays `passing` forever (20:17), and there is nowhere to put evidence but the `name` (Aug 8 10:12). ONE ROOT, TWO REPORTS, and the measured cost is in [[fact:defect-a-verification-has-nowhere-to-put-its-evidence-so-the-name-became-the-report]] — median name 79.5 words across 160 nodes, and I made four of the worst offenders TODAY.
2. AN INTERFACE CONSUMED ACROSS A BOUNDARY WITH NO SPEC RAISES NO GAP. Only `unprovided_interface` / `unconsumed_interface` exist. Their words: "a check reduced to 'an edge exists' can only ever detect the edge disappearing."
3. `open_questions` RETURNING 0 READS AS AN ALL-CLEAR. It returns a bare list while `loop_status` in the next call reported 31 other owed items. It is the orientation call a new session makes FIRST.
4. `disconnected_community` CANNOT SEE AN INTENDED-UNSATISFIED RULING, and proposes `generate_bridge` — precisely the forgery the ruling forbids.
5. A SEEDLESS SESSION CANNOT ORIENT. `detect_gaps`/`detect_defects` want a scope and `claim_region` wants a seed; a worker at check-in has neither. "The moment with the most time available is the moment the design brain is least usable."
6. `get_skill` CARRIES NO VERSION OR HASH, so a session that read a skill at minute 0 cannot tell it was revised by minute 90. Skills are served precisely so they cannot go stale, and this is the one hole left in that argument.
7. `import_graph` SAYS A DOCUMENT IS UNSTAMPED WITHOUT SAYING HOW TO STAMP ONE — so every adopt pass forfeits the upgrade-direction check.

PARTIAL OR UNVERIFIED: their prospective corpus-types entry (the ownership third is fixed; contradiction-resolved and the Fragment-for-unknown-intent shapes are unchecked); seat liveness after a `--stop-shared` bounce (`req:stale-seat-knows` is ACCEPTED and `mint_seat_liveness.rs` exists, but the orphaned-seat-after-bounce case specifically was not re-run); and the deferred-tool-indistinguishable-from-absent report, which is a HARNESS behaviour rather than a reflow2 one — though its consequence was real and durable, a false "there is NO mint_seat tool" travelling five hops into an onboarding doc as a credited correction.

⭐ WHAT THE FILE IS WORTH BEYOND ITS BUGS: it is a fleet reporting on its own tooling under load, and its best entries diagnose rather than complain — "a missing field being paid for in every future read of that node" is a better sentence than the defect it describes. Its no-consolidation rule earned its keep twice: two workers filed the `check-health` string ten minutes apart, and the duplicate is what shows the tool doing it to EVERYONE rather than one seat's opinion.
